q: Do PM Surya Ghar systems have to use Indian-made solar modules?
title: PM Surya Ghar domestic content rule
short: Yes. To get the subsidy, modules must meet the Domestic Content Requirement: modules made in India from cells made in India. MNRE's guidelines say using non-DCR modules in any form makes the installation ineligible. Check the module datasheet and invoice before you sign.

p: Solar modules in the installation must satisfy the Domestic Content Requirement, meaning domestically manufactured modules made from domestically manufactured cells, to be eligible for central financial assistance.

ul: The module make and model, and confirmation that it is a DCR module.
Serial numbers on the invoice, since documentation is uploaded to the national portal.
A system warranty: the scheme requires the complete system to be warranted for 5 years from commissioning, with 5 years of comprehensive operation and maintenance.

p: Where the modules are made changes the embodied emissions of the system, not the Scope 2 saving from the electricity it produces. Most buyers report the saving; product carbon footprints count the embodied part.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills, including net metering lines, so grid import, export and solar generation sit in one monthly record with the factor and source shown. Figures are self-declared.
